headline: Dropbox allows immediate API access for up to 500 external users in Development mode, but triggers a strict 2-week window to pass a mandatory review for Production status once 50 users are linked.
summary: Developers can create a scoped OAuth app to upload, download, and search files. The app starts in Development mode, allowing initial access, but reaching 50 linked users triggers a strict 2-week countdown to obtain Production approval. Production review requires an API usage description, privacy policy, custom icon, and adherence to least privilege scoping.

oauth.pkce: Supported and recommended for public clients via code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256
oauth.refresh_tokens: Supported. Pass token_access_type=offline in the authorize request to get a long-lived refresh token. Exchanged via grant_type=refresh_token.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Exact URI matching enforced. Must use https:// for production, http:// allowed for localhost/127.0.0.1 local development. Omitted URI defaults to out-of-band flow.
oauth.scopes: Space-delimited scope string in the authorize request. Must be enabled in the App Console first.

steps.title: Create app and configure OAuth
steps.detail: Register app in App Console, choose scoped access (App folder or Full Dropbox), get client credentials, and add exact redirect URIs.

steps.title: Implement PKCE and offline tokens
steps.detail: Implement Authorization Code flow with PKCE and token_access_type=offline for refresh tokens, then test API endpoints.

steps.title: Prepare and submit production review
steps.detail: Upload custom icon, add privacy policy, write detailed API usage justification, and request review in the console.

steps.title: Wait for Dropbox review
steps.detail: Dropbox reviews the submitted materials and grants production status to lift the 500-user hard cap and 50-user timer.

requirements.text: A custom application icon must be uploaded in the App Console.
A detailed API usage explanation describing how the app interacts with Dropbox and why permissions are required.
Justification of least privilege scoping, demonstrating why requested access levels (e.g., Full Dropbox vs App folder) are necessary.
A functioning privacy policy respecting user data.
Adherence to Dropbox Developer Branding Guidelines, including proper naming and avoiding implications of official partnership.

gotchas.text: Linking 50 users starts a strict 2-week countdown timer. If production approval is not obtained within two weeks, linking new users is frozen.
The app display name is permanently locked once approved for Production status and cannot be edited without contacting support.
Standard access tokens expire after approximately 4 hours. You must request token_access_type=offline during authorization to receive a refresh token.
Redirect URIs require exact matching and must use HTTPS, with the sole exception of localhost or 127.0.0.1 for local development.
Rate limits are dynamic and concurrency-based. Your application must parse and respect the Retry-After HTTP header when receiving a 429 error.

permissions.review_impact: Does not require a paid plan or administrator consent; standard Dropbox users can authorize. General production review is required to exceed user limits.

blockers.issue: New user connections are frozen after reaching 50 users.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Submit the Production status request immediately from the App Console, ensuring you provide a privacy policy, custom icon, and API usage justification.

blockers.issue: Refresh token is not returned during the OAuth token exchange.
blockers.how_to_proceed: Ensure your authorization URL includes the query parameter token_access_type=offline.

agent_can: Implement the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE.
Configure the authorization request to ask for token_access_type=offline for long-lived access.
Implement backoff logic to parse and respect the Retry-After header on 429 Too Many Requests errors.
Draft the API usage descriptions and scope justifications for the Production review.
you_must: Create the scoped app in the Dropbox App Console and provide the client ID and secret.
Upload a custom application icon and provide a valid privacy policy URL in the App Console.
Ensure the application name complies with Dropbox branding guidelines (e.g., does not use the word Dropbox).
Submit the app for Production review once eligible or provide justification for an early review.

key_claims.text: The OAuth discovery and authorization endpoints are active and enforce client ID validation.
Apps using solely pre-built drop-in components (Chooser, Saver, Embedder) do not require production review.
Dropbox does not charge fees for developer accounts or API usage, and does not mandate external third-party security audits (e.g., CASA/SOC 2) for standard OAuth API access.
Production review typically takes a few business days once submitted and eligible.

open_questions: How reliably does Dropbox approve early review requests for apps that have not yet reached the 50-user threshold?
assumptions: Hands-on time and time to first connection are estimates, not published by the provider.
Time to production includes both hands-on preparation time and the estimated provider review wait time.
